core_obligations: Reduce to comparing coefficients: fix an integral closed Z of delta-dimension k + r - 1, let Z' be the closure of its image, use the dimension bound to see that either Z' = Y, in which case both coefficients vanish because g composed with f is a unit over the generic point of Y, or Z' is a prime divisor of Y (proof lines 3112-3124).

Translate to local algebra: with xi' the generic point of Z' and xi that of Z, set A = O_{Y,xi'} and B = O_{X,xi}, note that A is a Noetherian domain, A -> B is flat and local and m_A B is an ideal of definition, and match the irreducible components X_j through xi with the minimal primes q_i of B so that the multiplicities become length_{B_{q_i}}(B_{q_i}) and the functions become the images g_i in kappa(q_i) (proof lines 3126-3144).

Reduce to a single length identity: writing the coefficient of [Z] in f^* div(g) as ord_A(g) length_B(B/m_A B) and the coefficient in the displayed sum as sum ord_{B/q_i}(g_i) length_{B_{q_i}}(B_{q_i}), and writing g = x/y, it suffices to prove length_A(A/(x)) length_B(B/m_A B) = length_B(B/xB) = sum_i length_{B/q_i}(B/(x, q_i)) length_{B_{q_i}}(B_{q_i}) and similarly for y; since A -> B is flat, x is a nonzerodivisor in B and the identity follows from the additivity statement for restricted divisors (proof lines 3145-3169).
proof_roadmap: Compare coefficients and reduce to the case where the image of Z is a prime divisor of Y (proof lines 3112-3124).
Translate both coefficients into statements about lengths over the flat local map A -> B (proof lines 3126-3154).
Prove the resulting length identity by additivity over the minimal primes (proof lines 3154-3169).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the flat pullback of the divisor of a rational function on an integral base of dimension k: it is the sum over the irreducible components X_j of the source of the multiplicity of X_j times the divisor of the pulled back function on X_j (statement lines 3097-3110, tag 0EPH). The proof compares coefficients after reducing to the case where the image of the chosen cycle is a prime divisor, then translates the two coefficients into lengths over a flat local map A -> B and reduces the whole statement to one length identity involving length_A(A/(x)) and length_B(B/xB), which is finished by additivity over the minimal primes of B. The translation into the local length identity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
